xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5599: Order books: the queue skips finished books

plan.title: Order books: the queue skips finished books
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: One derived rule (isBookFinished in currentOrderBook) has five readers that must agree: dispatch, the orders API, pan orders list, the Flywheel status summary and the page. Shipping any reader alone makes the page and the Flywheel name different active books. The 7 path-subsystems are src/lib, src/dashboard, src/cli, tests/unit and three single doc files; the code change is about 150 lines over 21 files.

narratives.Problem: The Flywheel releases work from the running book, else the first ready order book. A book whose issues have all landed still holds that slot, so the next queued book never starts until a person archives it. Separately, the dashboard issue cache drops closed issues after 14 days (issues.closedWindowDays), so a finished book would stop reading as finished two weeks later and a long book would never read as finished. Note: the 2026-11-22 July book (2026-07-30-hardening-20260729) still has three open issues, so it is not finished and this change does not release it.
narratives.Proposal: Add isBookFinished(progress) to src/lib/orders/phase.ts and pass it to currentOrderBook from every reader: dispatch (activeOrderBookIssues), deriveBookPhases (orders API and CLI), and the Flywheel status summary. A finished ready book is skipped, keeps status ready, and gets queuePosition null. Nothing is stored. Evidence stays fail-safe: only positive closed/parked state counts. The dashboard server backfills uncached issues of ready/running books through the existing IssueDataService.backfillIssue door (3000 ms cap) before deriving phases, and pan orders list prints the dashboard's phases when the dashboard answers for the same books. The page drops the finished-active notice and shows a finished queued book as skipped with Archive.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Writing any stored status when a book finishes
- Auto-archiving finished books
- Reordering the queue
- Skipping stale books that still have open issues (the July hardening book stays stuck)
- Fixing the deacon child's missing shared issue service or its labels-unavailable dispatch refusals
- Adding backfill or an HTTP read to activeOrderBookIssues
- Loading the issue cache in pan flywheel status
- Persisting backfilled issues to the SQLite cache
- Editing sync-sources/skills/pan-flywheel/SKILL.md or the PAN-5597 design mockup

autoDecisions.summary: Corrected the PRD's problem statement: the 2026-11-22 July book is not finished and stays stuck
autoDecisions.rationale: GitHub shows PAN-3290, PAN-3288 and PAN-3297 open with no parked label. The issue scopes the change to finished books; widening it to stale books would contradict the issue's fail-safe rule. Not a contradiction between authoritative inputs, so planning continues.

autoDecisions.summary: Added server-side backfill of uncached book issues through IssueDataService.backfillIssue with a 3000 ms cap
autoDecisions.rationale: closedWindowDays (14) drops closed issues from the cache; without backfill the skip rule silently reverts after two weeks. Verified live: a backfill of PAN-3295 moved the hardening book from 0/4 to 1/4 landed.

autoDecisions.summary: pan orders list prints the dashboard's phases when it answers for the same book ids, else derives locally
autoDecisions.rationale: The Flywheel loop picks the active book from pan orders list. A one-shot CLI keeps no backfill memo, so local derivation would name a finished book active after 14 days; getDashboardApiUrl already exists for CLI-to-dashboard reads.

autoDecisions.summary: Dispatch (activeOrderBookIssues) keeps the plain lookup; the old checkpoint CP-1 is decided, not delegated
autoDecisions.rationale: Its only caller runs in the deacon child, which never starts the shared issue service; the label gate refuses there before any book is read, so extra evidence would change nothing.

autoDecisions.summary: Finished non-active queued books get queuePosition null and sort after numbered queued books
autoDecisions.rationale: Numbers should describe the order the Flywheel will actually work in; the CLI formatter already prints 'queued (finished)' for a null position.

autoDecisions.summary: A running (legacy) book stays active even when finished
autoDecisions.rationale: Preserves existing behavior for data nothing writes any more; documented as the single FR-3 exception.

autoDecisions.summary: Set plan.metadata.sizeJustification instead of splitting into sibling issues
autoDecisions.rationale: Every reader must change together or the page and the Flywheel disagree about the active book; the subsystem count is inflated by three single-file doc paths.

items.title: Add isBookFinished and make currentOrderBook and deriveBookPhases skip finished ready books

narrative.Action: PRD WI-1. In src/lib/orders/phase.ts add exported isBookFinished(progress) = progress.total > 0 && progress.drained. Give currentOrderBook a second parameter isFinished: (book) => boolean defaulting to () => false, and skip ready books for which it returns true (a running book stays first even when finished, D3). In deriveBookPhases compute each book's progress once, call currentOrderBook(books, finishedOf), and number only the active book plus the unfinished in-queue books (D8): a finished non-active queued book gets phase 'queued', finished true, queuePosition null. phase.ts stays types-only imports (no resolver/cloister import). Update the module header comment. In tests/unit/cli/orders.test.ts replace the assertion expect(phaseOf(listLines(['PAN-1']), ids[0]!)).toBe('active (finished)') with ids[0] -> 'queued (finished)' and ids[1] -> 'active'. Add the tests named in PRD WI-1.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-3. Export interface OrderIssueBackfillService { isStarted(); issueIds(); backfillIssue(id) } and async backfillUnknownOrderIssues(books, { timeoutMs = 3000, service }) from src/lib/orders/resolver.ts. Default service adapts the lazily loaded issue-service module via loadIssueServiceModuleSync (isSharedIssueServiceStarted, uppercase identifiers of getIssues({ cycle: 'all', includeCompleted: true }), getSharedIssueService().backfillIssue). Return immediately when not started or when the cache holds zero issues. Otherwise backfill the uppercase issue ids of items in books with status ready or running that the cache lacks, awaiting Promise.allSettled raced against a setTimeout of timeoutMs; clear the timer; never throw. Tests use vi.useFakeTimers for the timeout case and an injected service; no real waits.

Add the route test that a finished first ready book is queued/finished/unnumbered and the next ready book is active, and the test that backfillIssues is awaited once with every book id in index order before the response.
